'''Luca Salasnich''' (born in 1967) is an Italian [[theoretical physicist]] and full professor of theoretical physics of matter at the [[University of Padua]]. His research concerns [[Many-body_problem|quantum many-body systems]], with a focus on [[ultracold atoms]], [[superfluidity]], and macroscopic quantum phenomena.<ref name="UniPD">{{cite web |url=https://www.unipd.it/en/contatti/rubrica?detail=Y&ruolo=1&checkout=cerca&persona=SALASNICH |title=Luca Salasnich – University of Padua profile |access-date=2026-04-21}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Salasnich was born in [[Padua]], Italy. He obtained a master's degree in [[physics]] from the [[University of Padua]] in 1991 and a PhD in physics from the [[University of Florence]] in 1995.<ref name="UniPD" />

Following his doctoral studies, he held postdoctoral research positions at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]] (1995), the [[University of Maribor]] (1996), the University of Padua (1996–1997), and the [[University of Milan]] (1997–2003).<ref name="UniPD"/><ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=https://materia.dfa.unipd.it/salasnich/curr.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae: Luca Salasnich |access-date=2026-04-02}}</ref>

In 2003, he joined the [[National Research Council (Italy)|National Research Council]] (CNR) as a researcher at the National Institute for the Physics of Matter (INFM).<ref name="UniPD" />

He became a faculty member of the University of Padua as an associate professor in 2011 and was promoted to full professor in 2021.<ref name="UniPD" />
At the University of Padua, he served as program director of the BSc in Optics and Optometrics from 2013 to 2021 and has been program director of the BSc and MSc in [[Materials science|Materials Science]] since 2024 (term 2024–2028).<ref name="UniPD" /> Internationally, he served as chair of the Physics panel of the [[Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO)|Research Foundation – Flanders]] (FWO) from 2022 to 2024.<ref name="UniPD" />

== Research ==
Salasnich works in [[quantum statistical mechanics]] and the theory of interacting many-body systems. His research focuses on ultracold atomic gases, including [[Bose–Einstein condensate]]s, the BCS–BEC crossover, and nonlinear phenomena such as [[Soliton|solitons]] and quantized vortices. He has contributed to the development of effective theoretical descriptions of low-dimensional quantum gases and nonlinear dynamics in superfluids, often using mean-field and beyond-mean-field approaches based on nonlinear Schrödinger-type equations.<ref name="CNRIRIS">{{cite web |url=https://iris.cnr.it/cris/rp/rp24214 |title=SALASNICH, LUCA |website=CNR Institutional Research Information System |publisher=Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche |access-date=2026-04-21}}</ref><ref name="PRA2002">{{cite journal |last=Salasnich |first=L. |last2=Parola |first2=A. |last3=Reatto |first3=L. |title=Effective wave equations for the dynamics of cigar-shaped and disk-shaped Bose condensates |journal=Physical Review A |volume=65 |issue=4 |article-number=043614 |year=2002 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.65.043614 |arxiv=cond-mat/0201395 }}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Salasnich was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2025 "for a broad range of theoretical contributions in ultracold atom physics, including analytical solutions to many-body equations, the physics of reduced dimensionality and curved configurations, and the analysis of collective modes, solitons, and quantized vortices".<ref name="APS">{{cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship/damop-fellowship |title=APS Fellowship – DAMOP Fellows 2025 |access-date=2026-04-02}}</ref>
From 2024 he is an ordinary member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]].<ref name="UniPD" /><ref name="EASAMembers">{{cite web |url=https://members.euro-acad.eu/ |title=Browse Members |website=European Academy of Sciences and Arts |access-date=2026-04-21}}</ref><ref name="EASAReport2023">{{cite web |url=https://euro-acad.eu/files/Jahresbericht_2023_Digital_v02.pdf |title=Annual Report 2023 |publisher=European Academy of Sciences and Arts |date=2024 |access-date=2026-04-21}}</ref>
